Architecture gaps: significant arrivals the registry does not map#

The registry (Model registry) maps an HF architecture only when a pinned backend's own code accepts it. It is generated from the pinned sources; nothing in it is typed in by hand. So "support" cannot be faked with an alias, and the census counts every other architecture as unmapped.

Alias or real work? Some unmapped arrivals are renamed or same-shape siblings of a supported family, and are fixed where the backend is (upstream, or our fork) by mapping the name. Others only look like a supported family. For those, mapping the name would advertise support that cannot be served, or silently compute something else.

This page is the reviewed evidence for the second kind: what each family is, what it adds over the closest supported architecture, and what real support requires. It exists so that: - nobody later "fixes" one of them with an alias; - whoever implements one starts from these measurements.

registry/significant.json lists the reviewed classes. tools/registry_build.py --check-gaps (ctest registry_gaps) fails if one of them becomes mapped without a recorded reason (mapped_ok must be a non-empty string; a missing, empty or vacuous value is still a violation), and the build prints the same warning. The census and pin-bump workflows run --check-gaps right after regenerating the registry, so a mapping lands nowhere without failing. ctest registry_gaps_fire (tests/registry_gaps_test.py) pins the guard's firing behavior against synthetic registries — registry_gaps on its own only ever sees a clean registry, so that test is what catches a regression that makes the guard stop firing. A pin bump that brings real upstream support then gets a person's look before the class counts as supported.

Provenance. The review was written for 1bit-MONSTER's own engine, before this repository (the 1bit-MONSTER census, 2026-09-12/13), and is kept as written below. The RCPP_ARCH_* names, rcpp_arch_from_string, registry/arch.h, src/*.cpp and census/* it cites are that engine's, not this one's. Where it says "the engine", read the old engine: englishbase, for example, was implemented there, not here. The configs, checkpoints and reasons are the models' own, so the conclusions hold here too: none of these is an alias of a family this engine's backends run.

deepseekv41 — DeepSeek V4.1#

  • Class / model_type: DeepseekV41ForCausalLM / deepseek_v41 (text tower deepseek_v41_text); example deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, Solstice-AI/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-UNCENSORED-FP8.
  • Shape: 40 layers, H=5120, 64 heads, 1 kv head, 384 experts, vocab 129280 — versus V4 Flash's 43 layers / H=4096 / 256 experts. It is a different model, not a revision label.
  • Keys V4 does not have: engram_* (8: engram_layer_ids, engram_num_embeddings, engram_vocab_size, engram_compressed_vocab_size, engram_max_ngram_size, engram_n_heads, engram_head_dim, engram_pad_token_id), candidate_block_size, candidate_source_layer_id, candidate_topk_blocks, index_source_layer_ids, kv_source_layer_ids. (dspark_* is not V4.1-exclusive — DeepSeek-V4-Flash-DSpark carries it under model_type: deepseek_v4.) It is also a multimodal wrapper (vision_config: deepseek_v41_vision, image_token_id).
  • Why an alias is wrong: src/deepseek_v4.cpp reads only hidden/layer/head/expert/hc_* scalars, so a V4.1 checkpoint would load through the V4 path and produce tokens while silently ignoring the engram and candidate-block machinery — the silent-substitution failure this repo bans, not a crash.
  • Why it is not mapped (rechecked 2026-10-23 on the pin main carries, third_party/llama.cpp af04c9f2, and again 2026-10-25 at 6b397ee9): the fork registers no DeepseekV41ForCausalLM converter class — conversion/deepseek.py has DeepseekV4ForCausalLM only — and src/llama-arch.cpp has LLM_ARCH_DEEPSEEK4 with the hc_* tensors but no deepseek_v41/deepseek41 architecture and no engram_* / candidate_block_* parameter. conversion/ reads neither key family at all. So tools/registry_build.py finds nothing to read the class from, and a mapping would load a V4.1 checkpoint through the V4 path and silently ignore the machinery above.
  • Watcher (engine #522): registry/significant.json carries "watch": "report" for this class, so the census prints it as REVIEWED and does not alert on every new upload of the family. That is a statement about the review, not about support: the class stays out of registry/architectures.json, tools/registry_build.py --check-gaps still fails if anyone maps it without a mapped_ok reason, and real support (engram embedding path + candidate-block sparse attention, plus a scope decision for the vision tower) needs the logits validation listed above.

  • Real support needs: shape-agnostic config + the engram embedding path + candidate-block sparse attention (and a scope decision for the vision tower), validated against reference logits from the HF implementation.

  • Mapped since 5e6388a5a (2026-10-30, the pin engine PR "Bump HRX: llama.cpp 5e6388a5a" carries): the fork now registers the class itself — conversion/__init__.py maps DeepseekV41ForCausalLM to deepseek41, src/llama-arch.cpp registers LLM_ARCH_DEEPSEEK41, and src/models/deepseek41.cpp implements the hparams, the tensor set, the graph and the engram/indexer machinery (fork #156, the port of upstream #31086 + #31300). That is not an alias of deepseek4: it is a second architecture, which is what the reasoning above asked for, and the recheck it quotes was against 6b397ee9, before the port existed. registry/significant.json records the same fact as a mapped_ok reason, so --check-gaps stays quiet.

qwen3mamba3 — Qwen3 + Mamba-3 hybrid#

  • Class / model_type: Qwen3Mamba3ForCausalLM / qwen3_mamba3; example arianraje/qwen3-4b-mamba3-hybrid-stage2b-kd-bias1.
  • Keys: layer_types (attention/SSM mix) plus Mamba-3 knobs — mamba_mimo_rank, mamba_bc_norm_eps, mamba_bc_bias_init, mamba_rope_fraction, mamba_a_floor, mamba_chunk_size, mamba_d_head, mamba_d_state, mamba_expand, mamba_n_groups, mamba_n_heads.
  • Why an alias is wrong: the engine has Mamba-1 (RCPP_ARCH_MAMBA) and Mamba-2 hybrids (FALCONH1, NEMOTRONH, GRANITEMOEHYBRID). MIMO rank, BC normalisation, an a_floor, and a rope fraction inside the SSM are Mamba-3 parameters with no Mamba-2 equivalent — mapping to a Mamba-2 path would compute a different recurrence.
  • Real support needs: a Mamba-3 SSM kernel + the hybrid layer loop, gated on decode validation against the reference.

molmoact2 — MolmoAct2 (vision-language-action)#

  • Class / model_type: MolmoAct2ForConditionalGeneration / molmoact2; example NUSMAGIC/MolmoAct2-MolmoAct2-SO100_101.
  • Text tower: text_config: molmoact2_text — 36 layers, H=2560, 32 heads, 8 kv, vocab 154624 (qk_norm_type, rope_scaling_layers, norm_after).
  • Not a text-only decoder: action_expert_config, flow_matching_* (6 keys), max_action_dim, max_action_horizon, action/state/depth token ranges — the model's contract is action generation, with depth reasoning.
  • Why an alias is wrong: the existing molmo → RCPP_ARCH_OLMO mapping is right for a Molmo VLM; here it would drop the entire action expert.
  • Real support needs: a scope decision first (text tower only, or the action path), then the action-expert/flow-matching head if in scope.

cosmos3edge — Cosmos3-Edge (video world model)#

  • Class / model_type: Cosmos3EdgeForConditionalGeneration / cosmos3_edge; example ubr-physical-ai/Cosmos3-Edge-NF4-bnb.
  • Text tower: cosmos3_edge_text — 28 layers, H=2048, 16 heads, 8 kv, vocab 131072, mlp_bias, pretraining_tp (llama-shaped). Alongside vision_config (cosmos3_edge_vision, num_channels → video patch embed), projector_config, video_token_id.
  • Why an alias is wrong: the text tower looks llama-shaped, but the model is a video world model; the engine has no video/image pipeline for it, so a mapping would advertise support for something that cannot be served.
  • Real support needs: scope decision (is video in scope at all?) before any mapping.

qwendriveforplanning — Qwen-Drive (driving planner)#

  • Class / model_type: QwenDriveForPlanning / qwen_drive; example Yuro1991/Qwen-Drive-1.0-4B.
  • Not a text decoder: the top-level config nests a vlm_config (Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration — the Qwen3.5 text tower plus vision) and an expert_config, and its own keys are trajectory planning: trajectory_hz, trajectory_point_dim, num_future_points, num_history_points, trajectory_scale, num_inference_steps, noise_init_std, min_one_minus_t, max_reasoning_tokens, plus id2label/label2id for two labels. Image geometry (image_patch_size, image_spatial_merge_size, image_temporal_patch_size, current_image_pixels, history_image_pixels) confirms a video/image input path.
  • Why an alias is wrong: the familiar part is the Qwen3.5 tower; the model's contract is a driving trajectory — a sampled (denoising) plan over num_inference_steps with a noise seed and min_one_minus_t, not tokens. The engine has no head or pipeline for that, so a mapping would serve the tower and silently drop the planner, exactly as with molmoact2 and cosmos3edge above.
  • Real support needs: a scope decision first (is trajectory planning in scope at all?), then the expert/trajectory head.

qwen3_5_mla — Qwen3.5 MLA attention variant#

  • Class / model_type: Qwen3_5MLAForConditionalGeneration / qwen3_5_mla; example TelperionAI/Qwen3.8-27B-GLA-g2-EXL3-4.0bpw.
  • Why an alias is wrong: the supported qwen35 path handles Qwen3.5's hybrid gated-delta-net/full-attention architecture; this class declares an MLA attention variant. The shared Qwen3.5 name does not establish compatible attention configuration or tensor layout, and mapping it to qwen35 would advertise unverified support.
  • Real support needs: verify the model config and tensor layout, then add and validate an MLA conversion/runtime path before mapping the class.

Uncovered classes reviewed later — same standard, and still not aliases#

The lane split above is the watcher's: a class is printed !! SIGNIFICANT when _is_significant() calls it a major-family/vision arrival, and !! UNCOVERED otherwise — and the alert's instruction for that second lane is "add the mapping … alias if it is a known family". The three below arrived in the !! UNCOVERED lane on 2026-09-13 and are not aliases either, for the same reason the sections above exist: a mapping would claim support the engine has not validated, and for englishbase it would be silently wrong rather than merely unsupported.

Evidence below is from the official HF configs and the models' own modeling code, fetched 2026-09-13.

englishbase — SlayerLab/fabryka-english-250m-e01-sft-v1#

Implemented 2026-09-13 — no longer an uncovered class (RCPP_ARCH_ENGLISHBASE = 1006, generic backend): the two-matrix relu2 MLP rides the non-gated FFN branch and the parameter-free QK-norm is the existing per-head path driven by an all-ones [head_dim] weight. Validated token-for-token against the model's own code — 68/68 greedy tokens over three prompts — with census/englishbase_parity_check.cpp. The review below is kept as the record of why it was not an alias, which is what decided the shape of the implementation.

  • Class / model_type: EnglishBaseForCausalLM / fabryka_english_base.
  • Shape: 36 layers, H=768, 6 heads / 2 kv, head_dim 128, intermediate 3040, vocab 32768, tied embeddings, rope theta 10000, rms_norm_eps 1e-6, qk_norm: true — llama-shaped on the surface, which is why the watcher filed it as a family variant rather than a significant arrival.
  • Decisive evidence — the model's own model.py: when recipe.activation == "relu2" (this config's recipe says exactly that) the block's MLP is replaced by ReluSquaredMLP, which computes down_proj(relu(up_proj(x)).square()) — one up matrix, no gate, ReLU² — and the same file describes its QK normalization as parameter-free. hidden_act: "silu" is only the default the Llama config class fills in; the recipe overrides the MLP at construction, so the two keys disagree and the code is what settles it.
  • Why an alias is wrong: Llama's and Qwen3's MLP is gated SwiGLU (gate_proj + up_proj + down_proj, SiLU), and Qwen3's qk-norm carries learned q_norm/k_norm weights. A mapping would load and then compute a different function — silent substitution, not a crash.
  • Real support needs: a two-matrix ReLU² MLP and a parameter-free QK-norm, or a loud refusal.

gdn2 — Berlm/hyb16-gdn2-s1#

  • Class / model_type: GDN2ForCausalLM / gdn2.
  • Shape: 24 layers, H=1024, 6 heads, head_dim 128, conv_size 4, hybrid — full attention on layers 3/7/11/15/19/23 — dense SwiGLU (2816), vocab 32000, tied embeddings.
  • The config schema is fla's (flash-linear-attention), not HF's: attn_mode: chunk, fuse_cross_entropy / fuse_norm / fuse_swiglu, expand_v, use_short_conv, allow_neg_eigval, and an ra_* block (ra_project, ra_gate_b, ra_theta_init, ra_lambda_max, ra_feedback) that no engine path reads.
  • Nearest implemented family, and why that is still not a mapping: the registry does have Gated-Delta paths — gateddeltanet / deltanet / tinygdn → RCPP_ARCH_QWEN3NEXT, and RCPP_ARCH_QWEN35 is Qwen3.5's dense GDN — but the engine's reader (src/qwen3_5.cpp) keys on Qwen3.5's own field names (linear_conv_kernel_dim, linear_num_key_heads, linear_value_head_dim) and on tensor names with expected sizes (linear_attn.conv1d.weight). This config supplies neither. A matching mechanism is not a matching checkpoint; an alias here would be a guess about weight layout.
  • Real support needs: an fla → engine config adapter, a tensor-layout check against one real checkpoint, and a decision on ra_*.

haiku — kerzgrr/Haiku-base#

  • Class / model_type: HaikuForCausalLM / haiku.
  • Shape: 36 layers, H=1024, 8 heads / 8 kv, layer_types = kda ×3 then gated_mla (full_attention_interval: 4), mlp_activation: "situ_glu" (situ_gate_cap, situ_up_cap), MLA ranks (mla_q_lora_rank 512, mla_kv_lora_rank 256, mla_qk_nope_head_dim / mla_v_head_dim 128), partial_rotary_factor 0.5, rope 1e6, and MTP heads (mtp_num_heads, mtp_adapter_rank, mtp_loss_weight).
  • Why an alias is wrong: KDA and gated MLA are named in the registry — RCPP_ARCH_KIMI_K3 is "Moonshot Kimi K3 — 2.8T MoE with KDA + Gated MLA + LatentMoE" — but that token is routed, not implemented: include/kimi_k3.h is included by nothing in the tree and its load_from_gguf prints [KimiK3] Loading not yet implemented for Strix Halo targets. and returns false; src/model_router.cpp has no branch for the arch, so it falls through to the generic hip_gpu → cpu_generic default; and situ_glu appears in no engine source — the only SITU in the tree is upstream llama.cpp's kimi_k3_situ. (That routing/validation split is deliberate and documented: issue #1635, closed as "not fixable on this box".) Mapping Haiku onto KIMI_K3 would chain one unvalidated class onto another.
  • Real support needs: a SITU-GLU MLP plus a real KDA / gated-MLA implementation — the K3 work itself, which research/TRACKING.md still carries as not started ("QK-Normed MLA absorption on Kimi K3 gated-MLA decode").

vapor — Neeze/Vapor-2B-V1.2#

  • Class / model_type: VaporForCausalLM / vapor.
  • It looks like the cleanest alias of the five. The config carries the LFM2 schema verbatim: every block_* and conv_* key identical to LFM2-2.6B, all 30 layer_types identical, hidden 2048, 30 layers, 32 heads / 8 kv, intermediate 10752, conv_L_cache 3. What is left over is packaging (dtype, auto_map, the tie_* pair), config-driven (vocab 128000, rope theta 1e7) — and one thing that is neither: an explicit rank_config.
  • The checkpoint is what disqualifies it (weights index read 2026-09-13): layer 0 stores the dense SwiGLU form — feed_forward.w1/w2/w3 — and layers 1–28 do not. They store feed_forward.A2, A_shared, B1, B2, B3 plus side_A2, side_A_shared, side_B1..B3: the rank_config's SharedSwiGLULinear (r_shared 1396, r2 1116, side_rank 8) realised in the tensors rather than a training-time detail that materialises on export.
  • Why an alias is wrong: the dense names the readers know (w1/w3, ~18 hits each in this repo) describe layer 0 only; A_shared, side_B1 and feed_forward.A2 have 0 hits anywhere in the tree. An LFM2 mapping would read the two dense layers it recognises and have nothing for the 28 factorized ones.
  • Real support needs: a materialisation (or runtime) path for SharedSwiGLULinear, alongside the plain dense block, then decode validation.

fidel — 4E-AI/Fidel1.1-1B#

  • Class / model_type: FidelForCausalLM / fidel.
  • Not a text transformer at all. Its 359 tensors live entirely under a policy. prefix and the stack is bespoke (from the safetensors header, read by range request — the file is 5.6 GB and was never downloaded):
    • policy.model.layers.N.mixer.mamba.* — 88 tensors: the per-layer mixer is Mamba, not attention;
    • policy.model.layers.N.moe.shared_fc1_gate / moe.w_gate — a MoE with shared experts;
    • policy.model.layer_adapters.N.base.{up,down} and .delta.{up,down} — the per-layer rank adapters the config's ranks block describes (base 512, delta 256);
    • policy.model.prompt_hyper_conditioner.* (78 tensors) and policy.model.prompt_cross_conditioner.*;
    • policy.model.contextual_prompt_v7/v8/v9.* and policy.chat_prompt.* — four separate prompt-attention blocks;
    • policy.model.lm_head.base.weight + lm_head.lora_a — the head itself is base plus LoRA. The header's own metadata agrees with the config: execution_contract: fidel_step9051_legacy_reference_fp32.
  • Why an alias is wrong: no engine family has mamba mixers + MoE + rank adapters + prompt conditioners, and layer_adapters, prompt_hyper_conditioner and mixer.mamba each have 0 hits in this repo. There is no partial match to argue about.
  • Real support needs: a scope decision first — this is a policy model, not a chat LM — and then the adapter/conditioner machinery.

zarya — ai-forever/Zarya-4B (also -1.7B, -0.6B)#

  • Class / model_type: Zarya / zarya.
  • Shape: 36 layers, H=2560, 32 heads / 8 kv, head_dim 128, intermediate 9728, vocab 151936, tied embeddings, rope 1e6 — llama-shaped on the surface, which is why the watcher's edit-distance guess proposed zarya → RCPP_ARCH_ZAYA.
  • Decisive evidence — the config is a diffusion LLM, not a Zaya MoE: the official config.json carries diffusion_attn_mode: causal, diffusion_loss_proportion: 0.5, diffusion_shuffle, noise_eps, noise_sorting, ordered_sampling, sample_t_override / sample_t_upper, grouped_noise — a full-sequence diffusion/masking sampler. RCPP_ARCH_ZAYA is "Zaya MoE (Zyphra — MoE FFN with CCA attention)"; the Zaya configs carry num_experts/CCA keys, none of which appear here, and Zarya has no expert tensors to route. The two differ in the one thing a rcpp_arch_from_string mapping cannot express: the computation itself.
  • Why an alias is wrong: mapping zarya onto ZAYA would route a diffusion sampler into the CCA-attention + MoE-FFN decode path — silent substitution, not a crash, exactly the englishbase / vapor failure mode above.
  • Real support needs: a diffusion-LM sampler (or a loud refusal), not a one-line registry alias.

The common thread: each of these is shaped like a family the engine already routes (llama, gdn, kimi, lfm2) — fidel only in the loosest sense, as a Mamba/MoE hybrid — and each differs in a mechanism that changes the computation, which is the one thing a rcpp_arch_from_string mapping cannot express. vapor is the case worth remembering: from the config alone it looked like a one-line alias, and only the tensors said otherwise.

Reading a checkpoint without downloading it. For a multi-GB model.safetensors, the header is enough to settle this class of question and costs one range request (follow redirects — -L — or you get the 302 body):

U=https://huggingface.co/<repo>/resolve/main/model.safetensors
H=$(curl -sSL -r 0-7 "$U" | python3 -c 'import sys,struct; print(struct.unpack("<Q", sys.stdin.buffer.read(8))[0])')
curl -sSL -r 8-$((8+H-1)) "$U" | python3 -c 'import json,sys; d=json.load(sys.stdin); print(len(d), list(d)[:20])'

<repo>/raw/main/model.safetensors.index.json answers the same question in one request when the model is sharded.

needle3 - webmp3/Sakura-Needle3-ONNX#

Architecture class Needle3ForCausalLM, model_type: needle3, no auto_map - so the census classes it as native, not custom code. It is a small research model shipped as an ONNX export; no pinned backend (hrx, npu) implements the class, and an ONNX graph is not a GGUF architecture any backend could claim. Reviewed 2026-10-06: not an alias.

sepia-char-mlp - LUSCAINK/SEPIA-0#

Architecture class SepiaCharMLP, model_type: sepia-char-mlp, no auto_map. Its config.json is not a transformer configuration at all (forward, vocab, embedding, hidden - a character-level MLP), so it cannot be an alias of any supported family. Reviewed 2026-10-06: not an alias.

kairo - kairo-crypto-model/kairo-v1.5#

Architecture class KairoForCausalLM, model_type: kairo, no auto_map - so the census classes it as native rather than custom code. Nothing in the pinned llama.cpp tree mentions kairo, and no pinned backend (hrx, npu) implements the class. Reviewed 2026-10-06: not an alias.

grug_moe - open-athena/Grug-67B-A2B-Merge-Campaign2-DARE-TIES-02-2026.10.10#

Architecture class GrugMoeForCausalLM, model_type: grug_moe, no auto_map, so the census classes it as native. It is the marin-community research MoE (marin-community/marin, experiments/grug/moe; lib/levanter/src/levanter/models/snowball.py): 67B total, about 2B active, 26 layers, hidden 2560, 20 heads with 5 KV heads, 256 routed experts (4 per token) plus one shared expert, a 2048-token sliding window with a global layer every 4 (global_every), and its own attention knobs (qk_mult, sconv, grugmoe_attention_mode). Transformers, upstream llama.cpp and upstream vLLM have no implementation; it is served through marin's own vLLM fork and loaded in training through marin-community/MarinSkyRL, which registers the class itself. The checkpoint flagged (engine#381) is a DARE-TIES merge-campaign upload with almost no downloads; the other uploads are the same group's training snapshots (open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-*, penfever/grug-67b-a2b-*). No pinned backend (hrx, npu) implements the class, and the qk_mult / sconv / local-global layout rules out treating it as a Mixtral- or Qwen-MoE alias. Reviewed 2026-10-12: not an alias. Its registry/significant.json entry carries "watch": "report", so the census watcher lists new uploads of it as . REVIEWED and does not alert; remove that field if an upstream backend gains the architecture.

hrm_text - zyr-AGENT/ZY-S1#

Architecture class HrmTextForCausalLM, model_type: hrm_text, no auto_map and library_name: transformers, so the census classes it as native, not custom code. It is Sapient's HRM-Text hierarchical-reasoning LM, in-tree in upstream Transformers (src/transformers/models/hrm_text/{configuration,modeling,modular}_hrm_text.py, "The Sapient AI Authors and the HuggingFace Inc. team"). The base sapientinc/HRM-Text-1B config (read 2026-10-15) is 128 layers of hidden 1536, 12 heads / 12 kv, head_dim 128, intermediate 4096, vocab 65536, rope 10000, num_layers_per_stack: 16, H_cycles: 2, L_cycles: 3, L_bp_cycles: [0, 3], embedding_scale 39.19, prefix_lm: true; the flagged upload zyr-AGENT/ZY-S1 (created 2026-10-12, last modified 2026-10-14) is a 16-layer finetune of it with the same H_cycles / L_cycles / L_bp_cycles.

Why an alias is wrong: H_cycles / L_cycles run a stack of layers (num_layers_per_stack) several times per token and L_bp_cycles feeds the low-level stack back through the high-level one, on a prefix-LM (prefix_lm, embedding_scale) schedule. No supported family does that: the closest decoder stack would read the same tensor names and silently compute a different function (each stack run once, no cycle), the silent-substitution failure this page exists to prevent.

Why it is not mapped: no pinned backend accepts hrm_text. Checked 2026-10-15 on the pinned submodule third_party/llama.cpp 0e255d77: no hrm in src/llama-arch.cpp, gguf-py/gguf/constants.py or convert_hf_to_gguf.py, and no conversion/hrm_text.py, so tools/registry_build.py finds neither a converter class nor a runnable GGUF architecture. The HRX fork's patched tip ad18320a is also free of hrm. Upstream ggml-org/llama.cpp master does have LLM_ARCH_HRM_TEXT ("hrm_text") and conversion/hrm_text.py, so a later pin bump that reaches it maps the class automatically - at that point tools/registry_build.py --check-gaps fails until this entry records why (mapped_ok).

Not a one-off. The HF hrm_text tag lists 60 models from 34 uploaders and the 2026-10-11 census snapshot counts 41 HrmTextForCausalLM models, including sapientinc/HRM-Text-1B (14,437 downloads, 834 likes) and danish-foundation-models/DFM-Mimir{,-v1.5} (2,175 / 2,824 downloads). Reviewed 2026-10-15: not an alias. Its registry/significant.json entry carries "watch": "report", so the census watcher lists new uploads of it as . REVIEWED and does not alert while no pinned backend can serve the class; remove that field (and record mapped_ok) when the llama.cpp pin gains hrm_text.

dflash2 - nchapman/Qwen3.5-4B-DFlash2 (also arc-kumbhar/incoai-Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2)#

Architecture class DFlash2DraftModel, no auto_map and library_name: speculators on the nchapman upload, so the census classes it as native and it alerts. Both flagged checkpoints are speculative-decoding drafters, not standalone LMs (nchapman's card: "DFlash2 speculative drafter for Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B"). The 2026-10-16 tensor headers (81 tensors each, read by range request) carry machinery no pinned backend runs:

  • candidate_selector.hidden_projection.weight, candidate_selector.predecessor_codebook, candidate_selector.successor_codebook - the candidate selector (selector_rank: 256, selector_top_k: 16);
  • layers.N.attention_conv.{base_kernel,kernel_projection.weight} and layers.N.mlp_conv.{base_kernel,kernel_projection.weight} - the short convolutions (conv_group_size: 16, conv_kernel_size: 2);
  • fc.weight, hidden_norm.weight, norm.weight and the per-layer attention/MLP tensors.

The pinned third_party/llama.cpp 1a5dcba2 does have a DFlash draft architecture (@ModelBase.register("DFlashDraftModel") in conversion/qwen.py, model_arch = MODEL_ARCH.DFLASH, runtime src/models/dflash.cpp), but that is DFlash-1. Its converter reads dflash_config.{target_layer_ids,mask_token_id} and the runtime requires target_layers metadata; it has no candidate_selector or *_conv tensors and no handling for selector_rank, selector_top_k, conv_group_size, conv_kernel_size, aux_hidden_state_layer_ids, sliding_window_non_causal or the speculators_config block. Registering DFlash2 under DFlashDraftModel therefore loads a draft that silently drops the selector and convolution heads - the silent-substitution failure this page exists to prevent - and the nchapman config does not even carry target_layer_ids under dflash_config, so the pinned converter could not build a GGUF for it at all. Reviewed 2026-10-16: not an alias. Its registry/significant.json entry carries "watch": "report", so the census watcher lists new uploads of it as . REVIEWED and does not alert; remove that field (and record mapped_ok) when a pin bump reaches DFlash2 support (selector + conv heads, per-layer window) and its converter class registers DFlash2DraftModel.

Architecture class DiacritizerModel, model_type: tashkeel_nano, no library_name and no auto_map, so the census classes it as native. It is not a causal LM: its config.json carries causal: false, num_classes: 15 (the diacritic labels), vocab_size: 171, hidden_size: 64, 18 layers, 2 KV heads, and a windows/decoding block (window: 256, stride: 128, arm: centered). The repo ships its own tashkeel_nano/ package (model.py, inference.py, labels.py), so the class is served by that code, not by any backend. No pinned backend registers tashkeel_nano and no supported family is a fixed-window, 15-class tagger. Reviewed 2026-10-16: not an alias. blind_decoder - Vi-LAB/KenT_0.5B_Base#

Architecture class BlindForCausalLM, model_type: blind_decoder, no auto_map, library_name: transformers, so the census classes it as native. It is the only upload (0 downloads, 0 likes, created 2026-10-16) and the repo is internally inconsistent: config.json declares architectures: ["BlindForCausalLM"] and model_type: "blind_decoder", but the shipped configuration_kent.py sets model_type = "kent" and modeling_kent.py defines KenTForCausalLM; BlindForCausalLM is defined nowhere in the repo and there is no auto_map, so stock Transformers sees an unknown model type with no remote code and cannot load it (upstream Transformers has no blind_decoder module). The architecture itself is bespoke, not a rename: 31 layers, embed_dim: 1024, 8 heads, vocab 50257, with Compressed-QK attention (q/k head_dim 64 against a 128-dim value head) and gated key refinement - k = softmax(G G^T / sqrt(d)) K_raw over a separate gate projection, before RoPE - plus RMSNorm and a SwiGLU MLP (intermediate 2816). No supported family computes that refinement; the closest decoder stack would read the same tensor names and silently compute a different function. Reviewed 2026-10-16: not an alias. Its registry/significant.json entry carries "watch": "report"; remove that field (and record mapped_ok) if a backend implements the class.

Architecture class NanochronoForCausalLM, model_type: sn38-nanochrono, no auto_map and library_name: transformers, so the census classes it as native. The repo carries no modeling code at all (only config.json, generation_config.json, model.safetensors, the tokenizer and a README), and upstream Transformers has no nanochrono/chrono module, so nothing can load it as published. Its config (read 2026-10-16) is 28 layers, hidden 1792, 14 heads / 14 kv, vocab 32768, layer_types of 3 sliding + 1 full attention per group, sliding_window: 512, max_position_embeddings: 2048, final_logit_softcapping: 15.0, attention_multiplier: 1.2, use_cache: false, tie_word_embeddings: false - plus machinery no supported family has: tap_layer: 14, aux_layers (every other layer), aux_gate_dim: 12 and mix_gate_dim: 24, the ChronoLLM/year-cutoff tap-and-gate stack the tags (chronollm, year-cutoff) name. There is no pinned-backend mapping and no alias to claim: the tap/aux-gate path changes the computation, so a plain decoder stack would be silent substitution. Reviewed 2026-10-16: not an alias. Its registry/significant.json entry carries "watch": "report"; remove that field (and record mapped_ok) if a backend implements the class.

muse_spark - Interchained/Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B-GGUF#

Architecture class MuseSparkForConditionalGeneration, model_type: muse_spark: Meta's Muse Spark Open (meta-models/Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B, created 2026-09-15, gated by manual approval), a 62-layer text model with vision and audio towers. The flagged upload is a GGUF conversion (F16, Q4_0, Q4_K_M, Q5_K_M) whose header (read 2026-10-17 by range request) declares general.architecture = muse-spark: 256 experts, 8 used, moe_latent_size: 4096 (experts run in a 4096-wide latent, like Nemotron 3 Super's ffn_latent_down/ffn_latent_up), expert_gating_func: 2, hidden 8192, 128 heads / 16 kv, head_dim 64, sliding window 2048 with one full-attention layer in four (sliding_window_pattern), final_logit_softcapping: 20.0, logit_scale 0.177, context 1,048,576, gpt-4o pre-tokenizer.

Why an alias is wrong: the latent-space experts, the per-layer rope schedule (layer_rope_theta 0 on the full-attention layers) and the softcapped logits change the computation; no supported family has that combination, so mapping it to a Llama 4 or Nemotron-H shape would be silent substitution.

Why it is not mapped: the pinned third_party/llama.cpp 1a5dcba2 has no muse-spark architecture (it has the moe_latent_size key and the latent tensors only for Nemotron 3 Super). Upstream ggml-org/llama.cpp added it on 2026-10-15 in ba3c05f71 ("model: add Muse Spark Open (text, vision and audio)", #30616: LLM_ARCH_MUSE_SPARK, src/models/muse-spark.cpp, conversion/muse_spark.py), after the fork's last upstream sync, so a later fork sync that reaches it maps the class automatically - at that point tools/registry_build.py --check-gaps fails until this entry records why (mapped_ok).

Not a one-off, but not servable here. The HF muse_spark tag lists 23 models (Meta's base and NVFP4, unsloth, mlx-community, intel-ai INT4, amd Quark-MXFP4). Even its smallest GGUF (Q4_K_M, ~500 GB) is about four times the 128 GB Strix Halo, so the gap costs nothing on the target box today. Reviewed 2026-10-17: not an alias. Its registry/significant.json entry carries "watch": "report", so the census watcher lists new uploads as . REVIEWED and does not alert; remove that field (and record mapped_ok) when the pin gains muse-spark.

glm5_next - azampatti/GLM-5.3-Flash-AZ (also zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash)#

Architecture class Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration, model_type: glm5_next, no auto_map and library_name: transformers, so the census classes it as native and it alerts. The flagged upload is a 4-bit auto-round derivative of Intel/GLM-5.3-Flash-W4A16-AutoRound; the release itself is zai-org's GLM-5.3-Flash.

Shape (configs read 2026-10-23, text_config): 45 layers, hidden 4096, 64 heads, vocab 154880, 288 routed experts with 4 used plus 1 shared (moe_intermediate_size 2048, first_k_dense_replace 3), DeepSeek-style MLA (kv_lora_rank 512, qk_nope_head_dim / qk_rope_head_dim, mla_use_nope), index_topk 2048 with 32 index heads, and num_nextn_predict_layers: 1 (MTP). The top level wraps a text_config plus a vision_config and image/video token ids, so the class is a VLM wrapper, not a bare decoder.

Machinery no pinned family runs:

  • layer_types is a 34 + 11 hybrid - 34 linear_attention layers (KDA: linear_attn_config.kda_layers, gate_lower_bound -5.0, short_conv_kernel_size 4, head_dim 128) and 11 deepseek_sparse_attention layers (full_attn_layers 3/7/11/.../43, all with indexer_types: full).
  • hc_mult 4, hc_sinkhorn_iters 20, hc_eps 1e-6 - hyper-connections, i.e. the residual stream is a 4-wide Sinkhorn-normalised expansion rather than one residual per layer.
  • index_kpool 4 with index_kpool_compress and index_kpool_always_select_tail - the sparse attention's key pool is compressed and a tail is always selected, which the fork's GLM-5.2 indexer does not implement.

Why an alias is wrong: the pinned fork's GLM-5.2 path (GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM -> LLM_ARCH_GLM_DSA, src/models/glm-dsa.cpp) is an MLA + DeepSeek-sparse-attention stack on every layer: it reads the MLA, indexer_top_k and indexer_types keys and assumes each layer runs that attention. The fork's KDA support is Kimi's (LLM_ARCH_KIMI_LINEAR, LLM_KV_KDA_HEAD_DIM, the Kimi converter), and nothing in the tree reads hc_mult / hc_sinkhorn_iters for a GLM model (only dsv4_hc_mult on DeepSeek V4 / qwen4exp). Mapping glm5_next onto glm-dsa would run 34 KDA layers as full sparse attention, drop the hyper-connection expansion and ignore the compressed k-pool - tokens out, a different function in: the silent-substitution failure this page exists to prevent. Mapping it onto kimi-linear would drop the DSA layers and the indexer instead.

Why it is not mapped: the pinned third_party/llama.cpp af04c9f2 has no glm5-next at all - no @ModelBase.register("Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration") in conversion/glm.py (it registers Glm4ForCausalLM, Glm4vForConditionalGeneration, GlmOcrForConditionalGeneration, Glm4MoeForCausalLM, Glm4vMoeForConditionalGeneration, Glm4MoeLiteForCausalLM, GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM, SolarOpenForCausalLM), no glm5-next in src/llama-arch.cpp's LLM_ARCH_NAMES (glm4, glm4moe, glm-dsa only) and no src/models/glm5-next.cpp. Upstream ggml-org/llama.cpp added it in #27773 (649dcb10, 2026-09-30, LLM_ARCH_GLM5_NEXT, src/models/glm5-next.cpp, MODEL_ARCH.GLM5_NEXT in the GLM converter) and the MTP follow-up PR #29928 (b9acf138, 2026-10-07) - both after the fork's last upstream sync, so a later fork sync that reaches them maps the class automatically. At that point tools/registry_build.py --check-gaps fails until this entry records why (mapped_ok), which is the intended prompt for a person to confirm the sync really brought the KDA + DSA + hyper-connection layers before the class counts as supported. Reviewed 2026-10-23: not an alias. Its registry/significant.json entry carries "watch": "report", so the census watcher lists new uploads as . REVIEWED and does not alert; remove that field (and record mapped_ok) when the pin gains glm5-next.

The same run also printed the REMOTE-CODE families KeuralMoECausalLM, LNewqForConditionalGeneration, Newq1ForConditionalGeneration and NewqForConditionalGeneration. granite_switch - ibm-granite/granite-switch-4.1-3b-preview (also -8b, -30b)#

Architecture class GraniteSwitchForCausalLM, model_type: granite_switch, no auto_map, library_name: transformers. registry/census.json (2026-10-29) counts 17 models of this class, so it is not a one-off: ibm-granite/granite-switch-4.1-{3b,8b,30b} are public and the family already ships GGUFs (ibm-granite/granite-switch-4.1-8b-GGUF, whose general.architecture is graniteswitch).

  • Shape: 42 layers (30b: 66), hidden 2560 (8b/30b: 4096), 40 heads / 8 kv (8b/30b: 32/8), vocab 100365 (8b/30b: 100355), every entry of layer_types full_attention, num_local_experts: 0 with a leftover num_experts_per_tok: 2 - i.e. dense, all-attention Granite.
  • What it adds: the model is a stack of LoRA adapters switched per token, not one set of weights. The config carries num_adapters, adapter_names, adapter_ranks, max_lora_rank, lora_target_modules, switch_head_dim, control_token_gain, dual_stream, cross_stream_rank, ms_code_*/ms_memory_gain, asr_* and adapter_token_ids/adapter_substitute_token_ids. Upstream's converter puts that in one sentence (conversion/granite.py: "Dense, all-attention Granite with N per-token embedded LoRA adapters, stacked over the adapter dim with a zero adapter at slot 0 (N = num_adapters + 1)") and additionally writes adapter_count, adapter_lora_rank, adapter_token_ids_*, adapter_router_gain and, for ibm-granite's decision adapter, a granite_switch decision type; num_hidden_layers also counts weightless switch layers that carry no tensors, and the converter has to derive the real block count from the tensor names.
  • Why an alias is wrong: the nearest supported families are granitehybrid (GraniteMoeHybridForCausalLM), granitemoe and granite, and none of their loaders has an adapter stack, a router gain or a switch layer: loading a checkpoint through them would keep one adapter's weights and silently drop the rest, which is the silent-substitution failure this page exists to prevent. Renaming it to granitehybrid would also lose the ASR path.
  • Why it is not mapped: the pinned backend has nothing to map to. At 40c4ccb7 conversion/granite.py:17-379 makes six @ModelBase.register calls covering eight class names (GraniteForCausalLM, GraniteMoeForCausalLM, GraniteMoeSharedForCausalLM, GraniteMoeHybridForCausalLM/BambaForCausalLM, GraniteSpeechForConditionalGeneration, GraniteSpeechPlusForConditionalGeneration, Granite4VisionForConditionalGeneration), src/llama-arch.cpp has granite, granitemoe and granitehybrid but no graniteswitch (nor granite_swa), src/models/ has granite.cpp, granite-moe.cpp and granite-hybrid.cpp and no granite-switch.cpp, and gguf-py has no GRANITE_SWITCH at all - as expected, since registry/architectures.json is generated from that tree.
  • Where the support is: upstream ggml-org/llama.cpp 157b81fe ("model : Granite-Switch Architecture", #25107, 2026-08-10) registers the class, adds LLM_ARCH_GRANITE_SWITCH / "graniteswitch" and the mapping case. That is older than the pin's tip (2026-10-25), so a fork sync is what brings it, and tools/registry_build.py --check-gaps then fails until this entry records why (mapped_ok) and someone confirms the loaded adapters really switch before the class counts as supported. Reviewed 2026-10-29: not an alias. Its registry/significant.json entry carries "watch": "report", so the census watcher lists new uploads as . REVIEWED instead of filing an issue; remove that field (and record mapped_ok) when the pin gains graniteswitch.

Unverifiable: gated configs#

A gated repository cannot be classified at all: the watcher's listing carries no config for it, so the class is unknown and the census counts it as unverifiable rather than guessing it. The watcher sends a token when one is in the environment. tools/census_watch.py's hf_token() reads HF_TOKEN, then HUGGING_FACE_HUB_TOKEN (the name huggingface_hub writes), and request_headers() adds Authorization: Bearer <token> when either is set and non-empty. No token file is read: the standard ~/.cache/huggingface/token is never consulted, so a token that only lives in that file changes nothing - export one of the two variables for the process that runs the watch (scripts/census-watch.sh passes its environment through to tools/census_watch.py). With neither set, the request is the user agent alone (1bit-census-watch), byte-identical to what the watcher always sent, and a gated row stays unverifiable: reported the first time it is seen, remembered in the state file, and never an alert, so it does not move the exit code. The header goes on the architecture walk's listing pages (hf_get_page) only; the FastFlowLM org listing, repo details and release pages (get_json) still send the user agent alone. A rejected token is not fatal: a 401 in hf_get_page sets _AUTH_REJECTED, warns the token was rejected (401); continuing without it on stderr, and retries that page anonymously, and the rest of the run stays unauthenticated rather than dying - a stale token costs a line of stderr, not the sweep. HF answers the listing 200 even with an invalid Bearer (measured 2026-10-29: GET /api/models returns 200 with a bad token, only GET /api/whoami-v2 returns 401), so that fallback is defensive: the watcher calls no endpoint that distinguishes a valid token from a bad one.

Long-standing: WaveMatrix/Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct-GPTQ-Int4 is unverifiable on every run.

From the 2026-10-27 census (engine#619): cestaristudio/granite-switch-4.1-3b-preview - the repo listing is gated (Access to model ... is restricted), so with no token in the environment the listing carries no config and the row stays unverifiable (reported once, remembered, no alert), not counted as an uncovered class. The class it would have named is no longer unknown: it is IBM's GraniteSwitchForCausalLM, reviewed from ibm-granite's public repos under granite_switch above, which is what the census now reports for that family. A token the repo has been granted access to puts the config in the listing and the row is classified like any other - !! UNCOVERED only if the pin does not map it; that has not been observed with a working token.

The 2026-10-22/23 watcher run behind engine#447 listed twelve, all unverifiable for the same reason - the watcher sent no token on that run:

Chandangepala/spendai-gemma3-1b, DrJohnCode/NebulaText, Elevatormusic/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017-2x-DGX-Spark-TensorFold-2x-Faster, ModaLeap/qwen3-4b-instruct-2507-onnx, ReadyArt/Wicked-Tutu-31B, dimitarpg13/semsimula-ladder-live-owt-d384-l2-attention-potential-rfqk-norc, executorch-community/Gemma-3-1B-IT-ExecuTorch-WebGPU, gostar77/qwen3.8-flash-next-radiance-q5-w5dn64-bf16ple, japanese-data-analyze/JMicro-10M-chat-research-20261018, seoan1024/Hanok-LLM, tasmaikeni13/algebraic-transformer, zendevvv/odoko-gemma3-1b.

None of them is evidence of an unmapped class: until a token is available they stay in the unverifiable count, which docs/registry.md reports separately from mapped and checked.

If a family is a variant#

An unmapped class that is a renamed or same-shape sibling is fixed where the backend is: upstream llama.cpp's converter and llama-arch.cpp, or our HRX fork. The registry picks the mapping up at the next pin bump. Verify shape equality before proposing such a mapping: layers, hidden size, heads, experts, and any added config keys. That check is exactly what moved the families above into this file.

Two classes flagged on 2026-10-14/15 are variants, not significant gaps, so they are deliberately not in registry/significant.json and keep alerting until a backend registers them:

  • GLMForCausalLM (JUROCLINIC/seguridad) is the all-caps spelling of the Transformers class GlmForCausalLM (model_type: glm), which the pinned fork already maps to chatglm (conversion/chatglm.py: @ModelBase.register("GlmForCausalLM", "ChatGLMModel", "ChatGLMForConditionalGeneration")). The registry lookup is exact, so only the CamelCase string is mapped; the flagged upload is a config-only repo (no weights) that also mis-cases the model_type. The fix is registering the alias in the fork's converter, not an architecture review - and it is only reachable via a pin bump, so it is not silenced here.
  • MinistralForCausalLM (saidutta69/Ministral-8B-Instruct-heretic) is a Mistral-shaped sibling: model_type: ministral, sliding_window 32768 == max_position_embeddings, and the same layer_types and 36-layer / H=4096 / 32-head / 8-kv shape as its base mistralai/Ministral-8B-Instruct-2410, which publishes MistralForCausalLM/mistral. The pinned fork maps MistralForCausalLM -> llama and Ministral3ForCausalLM -> mistral3 but does not register this name (upstream llama.cpp does not either). Same treatment: a converter registration picked up at the next pin bump, so it also keeps alerting rather than being recorded as significant.

From the 2026-10-27 census (engine#619), plus its 2026-10-29 rerun, four REMOTE-CODE families are recorded the same way - read and dispositioned here, deliberately not in registry/significant.json, and still what the census will alert on if a native (no auto_map) upload of the class appears:

  • LNewqForConditionalGeneration (crussella0129/LNewq) and Newq1ForConditionalGeneration (crussella0129/Newq1) are one rename each of the same Qwen3.5-VL wrapper: model_type: qwen3_5, text_config.model_type qwen3_5_text (32 layers, H 2560, head_dim 256, full_attention_interval 4, vocab 248320) over a vision_config with deepstack_visual_indexes, image_token_id 248056 - the shape the pin already converts under the name Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration (conversion/qwen3vl.py:16 registers that class and its MoE sibling; registry/architectures.json maps it to qwen35). The only unusual keys are lnewq_steer / newq1_steer, and both repos carry auto_map (AutoModelForImageTextToText and AutoModelForCausalLM -> modeling_lnewq.LNewqForConditionalGeneration / modeling_newq1.Newq1ForConditionalGeneration), i.e. they run their own modelling code. The pinned fork registers neither name, so the class - not the architecture - is what is unmapped, and the fix is one converter registration in the fork (a pin bump), exactly like the two classes above. The census counts one model each. The third name in that batch, NewqForConditionalGeneration (1 model, crussella0129/Newq), is now a gated repo, so its config could not be read on 2026-10-29; it is recorded as the same family name pattern, unverified.
  • KeuralMoECausalLM (hossain0909/keural-dpo2-final, 24 models from one uploader in registry/census.json) is not a rename of anything mapped: model_type: keural, auto_map to configuration_keural.KeuralConfig / modeling_keural.KeuralMoECausalLM, and the config is an MoE decoder the pin has no arch for (24 layers, H 4096, 32 heads / 8 kv, head_dim 128, 8 experts, top-2, sliding_window 512, vocab 131074, plus a keural_step key). No pinned converter or runtime reads that name, so mapping it would be a claim the engine cannot honour. It is left out of significant.json on purpose: it is a remote-code one-off until a second uploader uses it, which is why the census reports it as . REMOTE-CODE and starts alerting at REMOTE_CODE_SPREAD (3) uploaders - that alert is the prompt to review it for a variant shape, not to silence it now.
